chapter: Second lining and the brass bands
title: Musicians know him; pay for parades and a funeral call
summary: Musicians talk about White; he describes pay of two or three dollars a man, the seven-piece band and arranging a funeral parade at the hall.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I hear the musicians talk about you plenty.

That's me. And when they talk about me, that's who they talk about me. See, because all them, all the musicians from, I don't care where they're from. Mostly the musicians from, mostly they're where they leave from, from down here. And going up down, going up there and make, make a man out there self. But they don't have nothing down here. You see? You see, them time, that was two dollars a man. Two dollars or three dollars a man. For a parade, it might have been, it might have been more. You understand? For a parade, it might be more.
